pr_body:
This makes the interface more flexible, by allowing the same filtering
for show and status as is done for list-units.

Fixes #23207.
pr_comments: Do the shell completions need a tweak for this?

> Do the shell completions need a tweak for this?

I don't think so, because it's just extending coverage of existing options to new verbs. I don't think any of our completions are smart enough to know which verbs care about which options.
Maybe better to add a test?

In principle I'd agree, but we have exactly 0 tests for `--failed` or `list-units`, except for incidental use in other tests. We should add a full test for systemctl that at least verifies the main aspects of operation… But I don't want to be on the hook for that for this relatively simple pull request.
OK. Let's add tests later in another PR.

issue_context.title: systemctl status --failed, please?
issue_context.body:
To show more details about failed units and to avoid typing lengthy service names, something like 
```
systemctl status --failed
```
would be very nice. Currently (250.4) the "--failed" appears to be ignored (without usage hint).

Just a suggestion, of course.
comments: Sounds reasonable. The code is already there to filter units for `list-units --failed`, so it shouldn't be too much work.
what should this show other than "systemctl --failed"?

"systemctl --failed" hides the details. I noticed that I have to use "systemctl status failed.service" *every time* I have to examine a failed service. Why not show this immediately?

if services someweirdname1, anotherweirdname2 and yetanotherservice2fail failed, then "systemctl status --failed" should show the same as "systemctl status someweirdname1 anotherweirdname2 yetanotherservice2fail". 2 advantages:

- easier to type / no need for copy-and-paste
- lightweight way to get detailed information in **one** step

review_comments: Is it intended that we also always show a newline when we're following the `SYSTEMCTL_SHOW_PROPERTIES` logic path now? `show_one` seems to set `new_line` itself so it's weird that we just override it here now.
Yes. The newline separates the system status from the per-unit statuses. (And the per-unit statuses are also separated by an empty line.)
